audit.whatIsWrong: The page says three times that 'Zac's Q out-ranges your Rupture'. Stretching Strikes is 800 range and Rupture is 950 - the range advantage runs the other way. Separately, Unstable Matter is never mentioned at all, and no Zac ability is named anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Unstable Matter is the interaction that decides this matchup: a flat 5-second cooldown inside 350 units dealing a percentage of the target's maximum health as magic damage. Cho'Gath spends the whole game stacking exactly that stat, so Feast stacks increase the damage his W does to you. Telling the player to answer Zac with more health is the wrong instruction.
audit.corrected: Rupture opens from 950, outside his 800 grab and far outside his 350 W. Feast stacks feed Unstable Matter, so buy resistances alongside them.
sources: tools/audit-run/packets/chogath.json (defect: never names any of Zac's abilities)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both charts gave Cho'Gath levels 2, 3, first item and two items in a dead-even lane.
audit.why: The mirror audit at audits/top/zac__chogath.json establishes the calibrated chart for this pairing as Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Cho'Gath, and I am stating the same stages from this side so the two pages agree. The level-2 and level-3 claims also rested on the reversed range fact I corrected above.
audit.corrected: Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Cho'Gath with ratings 5,5,5,5,6,5,6. EVEN 6/10 stands.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named no cooldowns and described Cell Division only as 'blobs'.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9s - the longest cooldown in his kit and the one that actually gates his engage. Unstable Matter is a flat 5s. Let's Bounce! is 120/105/90s and knocks up four times. Cell Division's revive is on a five-minute cooldown, which is a fact you can track across a whole lane phase.
audit.corrected: Commit on Elastic Slingshot's 21 seconds; treat Unstable Matter's 5 seconds as a permanent tax on standing close.

audit.whatIsWrong: The itemisation advice is pure health, and the page tells you your Feast stacks answer him.
audit.why: Two of his abilities carry the percentHealth flag - Cell Division and Unstable Matter - so raw health is the stat he is best at punishing. Resistances and Grievous Wounds against the reabsorption do the work instead.
audit.corrected: Resistances alongside the Feast stacks, and anti-heal against Cell Division's reabsorption.

edits.before: Zac edges the early game because his Q out-ranges your Rupture and his passive turns the blobs he drops back into health you can't match, even with Carnivore ticking from last-hits. Don't throw a lone Rupture to poke; the cast delay lets him step aside, and if it lands he just walks up, Q-pulls you, and reabsorbs a blob to wipe the trade. Last-hit at max range, stand on every blob he leaves so he can't pick it up, and accept you concede Levels 2-3 while your combo and silence aren't online yet.
edits.after: Zac edges the early game, though not because he out-ranges you - Rupture reaches 950 and Stretching Strikes only 800, so you get the first cast. What beats you is Cell Division: every ability he lands sheds a chunk he can walk back over and reabsorb, erasing the chip you paid a cooldown for. Don't throw a lone Rupture to poke; the cast delay lets him step aside and grab you. Last-hit at max range, stand on every chunk he leaves, and stay outside the 350 units where Unstable Matter ticks.

edits.before: By Levels 4-5 your Carnivore sustain, Vorpal Spikes waveclear, and the Rupture-into-Feral-Scream combo stabilize the lane back toward even. The real swing is Level 6: Feast is true damage that ignores his blob-padded HP entirely, so it both deters his E slingshot dives and gives you a real execute. Bait the E engage, silence him with Feral Scream as he lands so he can't Q-pull or reabsorb, knock him up with Rupture, and Feast when he drops low; no amount of blob healing saves him from a true-damage execute.
edits.after: By 4-5 your Carnivore sustain, Vorpal Spikes waveclear and the Rupture-into-Feral-Scream combo hold the lane level. The real swing is level 6: Feast is 175-range true damage that ignores his blob-padded health entirely. Bait the Elastic Slingshot - it is 21 seconds at rank 1 - silence him with Feral Scream as he lands so he cannot grab or reabsorb, knock him up with Rupture, and execute. The discipline that wins this lane is staying outside 350 the rest of the time, because Unstable Matter costs you a slice of your maximum health every five seconds.

edits.before: This is where Zac reclaims it. He's a tank too, so your Feast-stacked HP doesn't out-class him, and his blob reabsorption plus R's repeated bounce knock-ups let him out-engage and out-last you in drawn-out fights. Your Feast still answers him in a clean 1v1, but he won't hand you one — he slingshots past you onto your carries and chain-CCs with Q and R. Win the lane before it scales there: bank early Feast kills off his over-eager E dives and deny his blobs so he can't snowball into the teamfight engage monster he becomes.
edits.after: This is where Zac reclaims it, and the reason is itemisation rather than engage. Unstable Matter deals a percentage of your maximum health every five seconds, so every Feast stack you bank makes his W hit you harder - health alone is the one stat that does not answer him, and resistances have to come alongside it. Add Let's Bounce! knocking you up four times on a 120-second cooldown and he out-engages you in the drawn-out fights. Win the lane before that: bank early Feast kills off his over-eager slingshots and deny his chunks.
